43:1: Surah Az-Zukhruf It is Meccan In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty says: “Ha Meem. By the clear Book” meaning clear, evident, and distinct in meaning and wording, because it was revealed in the Arabic language, which is the most eloquent language for communication among people. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Indeed, We have made it meaning We revealed it an Arabic Qur’an meaning in the Arabic language, eloquent and clear, that you may become righteous meaning that you may understand it and reflect upon it, as He the Almighty said: in a clear Arabic tongue. And His statement: And it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise He made clear its honor in the highest assembly so that the people of the earth would honor it, glorify it, and obey it. So God the Almighty said: And it meaning the Qur’an is in the Mother of the Book meaning the Preserved Tablet, as Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both and Mujahid said. With Us meaning with us, as Qatadah and others said. Exalted meaning of status, honor, and virtue, as Qatadah said. Wise meaning well-defined, free from ambiguity and deviation. All of this is a reminder of its honor and virtue, as God the Most High said: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an * In a protected Book * None touch it except the purified * A revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And He the Most High said: No! It is a reminder * So whoever wills may remember it * In honored pages * Exalted and purified * In the hands of scribes * Noble and dutiful. For this reason, the scholars may God be pleased with them inferred from these two verses that one who is in a state of minor ritual impurity should not touch the Qur’an, as mentioned in the hadith if it is authentic, because the angels venerate the Qur’anic copies in the highest assembly. The people of the earth are more deserving of this, because it was revealed to them, and it was addressed to them, so they are more deserving of meeting it with honor and veneration, and submitting to it with acceptance and submission, because God the Most High said: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, sublime and wise. And the saying of God the Almighty: Should We turn away from you the Reminder because you are a transgressing people? The commentators differed about its meaning. Some said that it means: Do you think that We will pardon you and not punish you, even though you have not done what you were commanded to do? This was said by Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Abu al-Saleh, Mujahid, and al-Suddi, and it was chosen by Ibn Jarir. Qatada said about the saying of God the Almighty: Should We turn away from you the Reminder? By God, if this Qur'an had been lifted when the first of this nation rejected it, they would have perished. But God the Almighty returned with His mercy and kindness, and repeated it to them and called them to it for twenty years or as long as God willed. The meaning of this statement of Qatada is very subtle, and the gist of it is that he is saying in its meaning that God the Almighty, out of His kindness and mercy to His creation, does not abandon calling them to goodness and to the wise remembrance, which is the Qur'an, even if they are transgressors and turn away from it. Rather, He commanded it so that whoever is destined for its guidance may be guided by it, and the proof may be established against whoever was destined for his misery. Then the Almighty said, comforting His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) for the denial of those among his people who denied him and commanding him to be patient with them: And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples meaning among the sects of the former people And no prophet came to them except that they used to ridicule him meaning they used to deny him and mock him. And the Almighty’s statement: So We destroyed those stronger than them in force meaning, We destroyed those who denied the messengers, and they were stronger in force than those who deny you, O Muhammad, like His statement: Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and stronger in power and the verses on this subject are very numerous. And the Almighty’s statement: And the example of the former peoples has passed Mujahid said: Their way. Qatadah said: Their punishment. Another of them said: We made them an example, meaning that we made them an example for those who came after them among the deniers, lest what befell them befall them, like the Almighty’s statement at the end of this surah: So We made them an example and a precedent for later generations, and like His statement, may He be glorified and exalted: The way of God which has already been with His servants, and the Almighty said: And you will not find any change in the way of God.

And His statement, And it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise He made clear its honor in the highest assembly so that the people of the earth would honor it, glorify it, and obey it. So God the Almighty said: And it meaning the Qur'an is in the Mother of the Book meaning the Preserved Tablet, as Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both and Mujahid said. With Us meaning with us, as Qatadah and others said. Exalted meaning of status, honor, and virtue, as Qatadah said. Wise meaning well-established, free from ambiguity and deviation. All of this is a reminder of its honor and virtue, as God the Most High said: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an * In a protected Book * None touch it except the purified * A revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And He the Most High said: No! It is a reminder * So whoever wills may remember it * In honored pages * Exalted and purified * In the hands of scribes * Noble and dutiful. For this reason, the scholars may God be pleased with them inferred from these two verses that one who is in a state of minor ritual impurity should not touch the Qur’an, as mentioned in the hadith if it is authentic, because the angels venerate the Qur’anic copies in the highest assembly. The people of the earth are more deserving of this, because it was revealed to them, and it was addressed to them, so they are more deserving of meeting it with honor and veneration, and submitting to it with acceptance and submission, because God the Most High said: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, sublime and wise. And the saying of God the Almighty: Should We turn away from you the Reminder because you are a transgressing people? The commentators differed about its meaning. Some said that it means: Do you think that We will pardon you and not punish you, even though you have not done what you were commanded to do? This was said by Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Abu al-Saleh, Mujahid, and al-Suddi, and it was chosen by Ibn Jarir. Qatada said about the saying of God the Almighty: Should We turn away from you the Reminder? By God, if this Qur'an had been lifted when the first of this nation rejected it, they would have perished. But God the Almighty returned with His mercy and kindness, and repeated it to them and called them to it for twenty years or as long as God willed. The meaning of this statement of Qatada is very subtle, and the gist of it is that he is saying in its meaning that God the Almighty, out of His kindness and mercy to His creation, does not abandon calling them to goodness and to the wise remembrance, which is the Qur'an, even if they are transgressors and turn away from it. Rather, He commanded it so that whoever is destined for its guidance may be guided by it, and the proof may be established against whoever was destined for his misery. Then the Almighty said, comforting His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) for the denial of those among his people who denied him and commanding him to be patient with them: And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples meaning among the sects of the former people And no prophet came to them except that they used to ridicule him meaning they used to deny him and mock him. And the Almighty’s statement: So We destroyed those stronger than them in force meaning, We destroyed those who denied the messengers, and they were stronger in force than those who deny you, O Muhammad, like His statement: Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and stronger in power and the verses on this subject are very numerous. And the Almighty’s statement: And the example of the former peoples has passed Mujahid said: Their way. Qatadah said: Their punishment. Another of them said: We made them an example, meaning that we made them an example for those who came after them among the deniers, lest what befell them befall them, like the Almighty’s statement at the end of this surah: So We made them an example and a precedent for later generations, and like His statement, may He be glorified and exalted: The way of God which has already been with His servants, and the Almighty said: And you will not find any change in the way of God.
43:9: God Almighty says: And if you, O Muhammad, ask these polytheists who worship other than Him, Who created the heavens and the earth? they will surely say, The Exalted in Might, the Knowing created them. That is, they will acknowledge that the Creator of that is God alone, with no partner for Him, and yet they worship other idols and rivals with Him. Then God Almighty says: He who made the earth a cradle for you, that is, a stable, settled bed on which you walk, stand, sleep, and depart, even though it was created on a stream of water. But He anchored it with mountains so that it would not shake this way or that. And He made for you paths therein, that is, roads between the mountains and valleys, that you may be guided, that is, in your travel from one country to another, and one region to another. And He who sends down water from the sky in due measure, that is, according to what is sufficient for your crops, fruits, and drinking for yourselves and your livestock. And the words of the Most High: Then We revived thereby a dead land, meaning a dead land. When the water came to it, it quivered and swelled and produced every beautiful pair. Then the Most High pointed out by reviving the land the revival of bodies on the Day of Resurrection after their death, saying: Thus you will be brought forth. Then the Almighty said: And He who created all pairs, meaning from what the earth produces of all kinds of plants, crops, fruits, flowers, and other things. And from the animals of different kinds and types, And He has made for you of the ships meaning the ships and the grazing livestock that which you ride meaning He has tamed them for you and made them subservient and made them easy for you to eat their meat and drink their milk and ride their backs. For this reason, the Most High said: That you may mount upon their backs meaning that you may mount firmly and elevated upon their backs meaning on the backs of this kind then remember the favor of your Lord meaning in what He has subjected to you when you are mounted upon it and say, ‘Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it’ meaning that we could not have resisted it. And if God had not subjected this to us, we would not have been able to do it. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: Muqrinin means able to do so. “And indeed, to our Lord we will return” means we will go to Him after our death, and to Him is our greater journey. This is by way of drawing attention to the course of this world and the course of the Hereafter, just as He drew attention to the provision for the Hereafter with worldly provisions in His Almighty’s saying: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. And to the clothing for this world and the clothing for the Hereafter in His Almighty’s saying: “And adornments. And the clothing of righteousness - that is best.” Mentioning the hadiths related to riding an animal Hadith of the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him. The Imam said: Yazid told us, Sharik ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi’ah, who said: I saw Ali, may God be pleased with him, brought a mount. When he put his foot in the stirrup, he said: In the name of God. When he mounted it, he said: Praise be to God. “Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return.” Then he praised God three times and said: “Glory be to You, there is no god but You. I have wronged myself, so forgive me.” Then he laughed. I said to him: Why did you laugh, O Commander of the Faithful? He, may God be pleased with him, said: “I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do as I did, then he laughed.” I said: Why did you laugh, O Messenger of God? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, is pleased with His servant when he says, ‘O Lord, forgive me.’ He says, ‘My servant knows that no one forgives sins except Me.’ This is how it was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas. Al-Nasa’i and Mansur added on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi’ah al-Asadi al-Walibi, with this chain of transmission. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi said on the authority of Shu’bah: I said to Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i: ‘From whom did you hear this hadith?’ He said: ‘From Yunus ibn Khabab.’ So I met Yunus ibn Khabab and said: ‘From whom did you hear it?’ He said: ‘From a man who heard it from Ali ibn Rabi’ah.’ Some of them narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of Shaqiq ibn Uqbah al-Asadi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi’ah al-Walibi, with this chain of transmission. Hadith of Abdullah bin Abbas may God be pleased with them both. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, “Abu Bakr bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had him ride behind him on his mount. When he had mounted it, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said God is Most Great three times, and Al-Hamdulillah three times, and Laa ilaaha ill-God once. Then he lay down on it and laughed, then he turned to him and said, ‘There is no Muslim man who rides and does as you have done, except that God, the Almighty, turns to him and laughs at him as I laughed at you.’” It was transmitted only by Ahmad. Hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Ali ibn Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would mount his camel, he would say Allahu Akbar three times, then say: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, for we could not have subdued it, and indeed, to our Lord we will return. Then he would say: “O God, I ask You in this journey of mine for righteousness and piety, and for deeds that please You. O God, make the journey easy for us and shorten for us what is far away. O God, You are the Companion in travel and the Successor over the family. O God, be our companion in our journey and take care of our families.” And when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would return to his family, he would say: We are returning, repentant, God willing, worshipping and praising our Lord. Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa’i narrated this in this way from Ibn Jurayj, and at-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, both on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr with this chain. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Hakam ibn Thauban, on the authority of Abu Las al-Khuza’i, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, carried us on camels from the charity camels to Hajj, and we said: O Messenger of God, we do not think that we should carry these, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no camel but that there is a devil on its mount, so mention the name of God over it when you ride it as I command you, then treat it with kindness for yourselves, for only God Almighty carries.” Abu Las’ name is Muhammad ibn al-Aswad ibn Khalaf. Another hadith with the same meaning - Ahmad said: Atab told us, Abdullah and Ali bin Ishaq told us, Abdullah - meaning Ibn al-Mubarak - told us, Usama bin Zaid told us, Muhammad bin Hamza told me that he heard his father say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: On the back of every camel is a devil, so when you mount it, say the name of God Almighty and then do not neglect your needs.

43:15: God the Almighty says, informing about the polytheists in what they fabricated and lied about, in that they made some of the livestock up for their idols and some for God the Almighty, as God the Almighty mentioned about them in Surat Al-An'am in His saying, the Blessed and Most High: “And they have assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock, and they say, ‘This is for God,’ according to their claim, and this is for our associates. So whatever is for their associates does not reach God, and whatever is for God reaches their associates. Evil is that which they judge.” And likewise, they assigned to Him, in the division of daughters and sons, the worst and most degrading of the two, which is daughters, as God the Almighty said: Do you have males and He has females? That would then be an unfair division. And He the Almighty said here: “And they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.” Then He the Almighty said: Or has He taken from what He creates daughters and preferred you with sons? This is the utmost denial of them. Then He mentioned the complete denial, as He, the Most High, said: And when one of them is given the report of that which is presented as an example for the Most Merciful, his face darkens, and he is filled with inward grief. That is, when one of these people is given the report of the daughters they have attributed to God, he is extremely disgusted by that, and is overcome by depression because of the bad report he has received, and he hides from the people out of shame because of that. God Almighty says: How can you be disgusted by that and attribute it to God Almighty? Then He, the Most High, said: Or one who grows up in adornment and is in dispute not clear? That is, a woman is deficient, and her deficiency is completed by wearing jewelry from the time she is a child, and if she disputes, she has no expression, rather she is helpless and unable. Or is someone like this attributed to the presence of the Almighty God? The female is deficient in appearance and in essence, in form and meaning, so the deficiency of her appearance and image is completed by wearing jewelry and what is similar to it to make up for her deficiency, as some Arab poets said: Jewelry is nothing but an adornment for a deficiency that completes beauty if beauty is limited. But if beauty is abundant like your beauty, there is no need to visit. As for the deficiency of its meaning, it is weak and unable to triumph when triumphant, it has no expression or ambition, as some Arabs said when he was given the good report of a daughter: She is not a blessing of a son, her victory is crying, and her righteousness is theft. And the saying of the Blessed and Most High: And they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females means they believed that about them, so the Most High denounced their saying that and said: Witness their creation meaning they witnessed it and God created them females. Their testimony will be recorded meaning about that and they will be questioned about that on the Day of Resurrection, and this is a severe threat and a definite warning. And they said, ‘If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them’ meaning if God had willed, He would have prevented us from worshipping these idols that are in the form of the angels who are the daughters of God, for He knows that and He approves of it for us. So they combined many types of error: One of them is that they made God Almighty a son, and He is exalted, sanctified, and far above that, greatly exalted. Second Their claim that He chose daughters over sons, so they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females. Third Their worship of them, despite all of this, is without evidence, proof, or permission from God Almighty, but rather based on mere opinions, whims, imitation of ancestors, notables, fathers, and the ignorant wandering in ignorance. Fourth Their argument is based on their own estimation of that. They are very ignorant in this argument, for God the Almighty has vehemently denied that to them. For ever since He sent the messengers and revealed the books, He has commanded us to worship Him alone, with no partner or associate, and has forbidden us from worshipping anyone other than Him. God the Almighty says: “And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ And among them were those whom God guided, and among them were those upon whom error was justified. So travel through the land and observe what was the end of those who denied.” And God the Almighty says: “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: ‘Did We appoint other than the Most Merciful deities to be worshipped?’” And God the Almighty says in this verse, after mentioning their argument: They have no knowledge of that, meaning the truth of what they said and the argument they used. They are only guessing, meaning they lie and fabricate. Mujahid said about God’s statement: “They have no knowledge of that. They are only guessing,” meaning they do not know God’s ability to do that.

Then see how was the end of the deniers, meaning how they perished and were destroyed, and how God saved the believers.

43:26: The Almighty says, informing about His servant, messenger, and friend, the leader of the monotheists and the father of the prophets sent after him, to whom the Quraysh trace their lineage and doctrine, that he disavowed his father and his people in their worship of idols, saying: “Indeed, I am disassociated from what you worship, except for He who created me, and indeed, He will guide me. And He made it a word remaining among his posterity,” meaning this word, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner, and the abandonment of all idols other than Him, and it is there is no god but God, meaning He made it permanent in his posterity, so that those whom God Almighty guided from the descendants of Abraham, peace be upon him, would follow his example in it, so that they might return, meaning to it. 43:34: The Almighty says, informing about His servant, messenger, and friend, the leader of the monotheists and the father of the prophets sent after him, to whom the Quraysh trace their lineage and doctrine, that he disavowed his father and his people in their worship of idols, saying: “Indeed, I am disassociated from what you worship, except for He who created me, and indeed, He will guide me. Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, As-Suddi and others said regarding the words of God the Almighty: {And made it a word remaining among his posterity} meaning, There is no god but God, and among his posterity there will not cease to say it. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both. Ibn Zayd said: The word of Islam, and it goes back to what the group said. Then God the Almighty said: {Rather, You gave enjoyment to these} meaning the polytheists, {and their fathers} meaning, their lives were prolonged in their misguidance, {until there came to them the truth and a clear Messenger} meaning, he explained the message and the warning. {And when the truth came to them, they said, This is magic, and indeed, we are disbelievers in it.} meaning, they denied it and opposed it and repelled it with their hearts and souls out of disbelief, envy and malice. {And they said} meaning, like objectors to the One Who sent it down, {Why was this Qur’an not sent down to some important man from the two cities?} meaning, why was this Qur’an not sent down to some important man from the two cities? They mean Makkah and Taif, said Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Ikrimah, Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, Qatadah, As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. More than one of them mentioned that they meant Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and Urwah bin Masoud Ath-Thaqafi. Malik said on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi: They mean Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and Masoud bin Amr Ath-Thaqafi. Mujahid said: They mean Utbah bin Rabi’ah. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: A tyrant from the tyrants of Quraysh. He may God be pleased with him said: They meant Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and Habib bin Amr bin Umair Ath-Thaqafi. Mujahid said: They meant Utbah bin Rabi’ah in Makkah and Ibn Abd Yalil in At-Taif. As-Suddi said: They meant Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and Kinanah bin Amr bin Umair Ath-Thaqafi. It appears that they meant an important man from whichever of the two towns he was. God the Almighty said in response to their objection: Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? That is, the matter is not up to them. Rather, it is up to God Almighty, and God knows best where to place His messages, for He only sends them down to the purest of creation in heart and soul, the most honorable of households, and the purest of origins. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih.

43:36: God the Almighty says: And whoever is blind that is, pretends to be blind, neglects, and turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful. Blindness in the eye is the weakness of its sight, and what is meant here is blindness of insight. We appoint for him a devil who is to him a companion, like the Almighty’s statement: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him (al-An’am 2:17), and like His statement: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate (al-An’am 2:17), and like His statement, the Most High: And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them (al-An’am 2:17). For this reason the Almighty said here: And indeed, they avert them from the way while they think that they are guided * Until, when there comes to Us (al-An’am 2:17), that is, this one who neglected guidance, We appoint for him a devil who misleads him and guides him to the path of Hellfire. So when he meets God the Almighty on the Day of Resurrection, he will be fed up with the devil who was assigned to him. He will say, ‘Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts, what an evil companion!’ Some of them read, Until he comes to Us, meaning the companion and the one who is paired. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Saeed al-Jariry, who said: It has reached us that when the disbeliever is raised from his grave on the Day of Resurrection, a devil will strike him with his hand and will not leave him until God the Almighty sends them both to the Fire. That is when he will say, Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts, what an evil companion! What is meant by the two easts here is what is between the east and the west, and it is used here for emphasis, just as one says: the two moons, the two lives, and the two parents, as Ibn Jarir and others said. Then God the Almighty said: {And it will not benefit you this Day, since you have wronged, that you are sharers in the punishment} meaning, your gathering in the Fire and your sharing in the painful punishment will not benefit you. And God the Almighty said: {Then can you make the deaf hear or guide the blind and him who is in manifest error} meaning, that is not up to you. Rather, your responsibility is to convey the message, not their guidance. Rather, God guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills, and He is the Just Judge in that. Then God the Almighty said: {Then whether We take you away - indeed, We will take retribution from them} meaning, We will inevitably take retribution from them and punish them, even if you were to go away. {Or We show you what We have promised them - indeed, We are over them powerful} meaning, We are able to do this and that. And God the Almighty did not take His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until He had satisfied his eyes against his enemies, and had control over their forelocks, and had dominion over what their forelocks contained! This is the meaning of Al-Suddi’s statement, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, who said: Qatada recited: If We should take you away, We will surely take retribution from them. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has gone, but the retribution remains. God Almighty will not show His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, anything he dislikes in his nation until he passes away. There has never been a prophet who did not see punishment in his nation, except your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shown what would befall his nation after him, and he was never seen laughing or smiling until God, the Almighty, took him. He mentioned a narration from Saeed bin Abi Arubah on the authority of Qatadah, similar to this, then Ibn Jarir narrated something similar to that from Al-Hasan as well. And in the hadith: “The stars are a security for the heavens, so when the stars go, the heavens will be threatened with what is promised. And I am a security for my companions, so when I go, my companions will be threatened with what is promised.” Then God, the Almighty, said: So hold fast to that which has been revealed to you, for you are on a straight path. That is, take the Qur’an revealed to your heart, for it is the truth, and what it guides to is the truth that leads to the straight path of God, which leads to the gardens of bliss and everlasting good. Then He, the Most High, said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people. It was said that its meaning is It is an honor for you and your people. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said this. Ibn Jarir chose it and did not narrate anything else. Al-Baghawi included here the hadith of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im on the authority of Mu’awiyah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “This matter is in the hands of the Quraysh. No one will dispute it with them except that God, the Most High, will throw him down on his face as long as they establish the religion.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Its meaning is that it is an honor for them in that it was revealed in their language. They are the most knowledgeable of it, so they should be the most upright of people in it and the most effective in implementing it. This is how their best and elite were from among the sincere ones from among the first and foremost emigrants and those who resembled them and followed them. It was said that its meaning is And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, meaning a reminder for you and your people. And singling them out for mention does not exclude others, like the Most High’s saying: “Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance. Will you not then reason?” And like His saying, the Most High, the Most Blessed: And warn your nearest relatives “and you will be questioned” about this Qur’an, and how you acted upon it and responded to it. God the Almighty said: “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: ‘Did We appoint other than the Most Merciful gods to be worshipped?’” That is, all the messengers called people to what you called people to, namely the worship of God alone, with no partner or associate, and they forbade the worship of idols and rivals, as God the Almighty said: And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ Mujahid said regarding the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him: And ask those to whom We sent before you of Our messengers. Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi narrated it in this way from Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him. This is as if it is an explanation, not a recitation, and God knows best. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: “And ask them on the Night of the Isra’ Journey to Heaven, for the prophets (peace and blessings be upon them) gathered for it.” Ibn Jarir chose the first, and God knows best.

We appoint for him a devil who is to him a companion, like the Almighty’s statement: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him (al-An’am 2:17), and like His statement: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate (al-An’am 2:17), and like His statement, the Most High: And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them (al-An’am 2:17). For this reason the Almighty said here: And indeed, they avert them from the way while they think that they are guided * Until, when there comes to Us (al-An’am 2:17), that is, this one who neglected guidance, We appoint for him a devil who misleads him and guides him to the path of Hellfire. So when he meets God the Almighty on the Day of Resurrection, he will be fed up with the devil who was assigned to him. He will say, ‘Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts, what an evil companion!’ Some of them read, Until he comes to Us, meaning the companion and the one who is paired. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Saeed al-Jariry, who said: It has reached us that when the disbeliever is raised from his grave on the Day of Resurrection, a devil will strike him with his hand and will not leave him until God the Almighty sends them both to the Fire. That is when he will say, Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts, what an evil companion! What is meant by the two easts here is what is between the east and the west, and it is used here for emphasis, just as one says: the two moons, the two lives, and the two parents, as Ibn Jarir and others said. Then God the Almighty said: {And it will not benefit you this Day, since you have wronged, that you are sharers in the punishment} meaning, your gathering in the Fire and your sharing in the painful punishment will not benefit you. And God the Almighty said: {Then can you make the deaf hear or guide the blind and him who is in manifest error} meaning, that is not up to you. Rather, your responsibility is to convey the message, not their guidance. Rather, God guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills, and He is the Just Judge in that. Then God the Almighty said: {Then whether We take you away - indeed, We will take retribution from them} meaning, We will inevitably take retribution from them and punish them, even if you were to go away. {Or We show you what We have promised them - indeed, We are over them powerful} meaning, We are able to do this and that. And God the Almighty did not take His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until He had satisfied his eyes against his enemies, and had control over their forelocks, and had dominion over what their forelocks contained! This is the meaning of Al-Suddi’s statement, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, who said: Qatada recited: If We should take you away, We will surely take retribution from them. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has gone, but the retribution remains. God Almighty will not show His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, anything he dislikes in his nation until he passes away. There has never been a prophet who did not see punishment in his nation, except your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shown what would befall his nation after him, and he was never seen laughing or smiling until God, the Almighty, took him. He mentioned a narration from Saeed bin Abi Arubah on the authority of Qatadah, similar to this, then Ibn Jarir narrated something similar to that from Al-Hasan as well. And in the hadith: “The stars are a security for the heavens, so when the stars go, the heavens will be threatened with what is promised. And I am a security for my companions, so when I go, my companions will be threatened with what is promised.” Then God, the Almighty, said: So hold fast to that which has been revealed to you, for you are on a straight path. That is, take the Qur’an revealed to your heart, for it is the truth, and what it guides to is the truth that leads to the straight path of God, which leads to the gardens of bliss and everlasting good. Then He, the Most High, said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people. It was said that its meaning is It is an honor for you and your people. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said this. Ibn Jarir chose it and did not narrate anything else. Al-Baghawi included here the hadith of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im on the authority of Mu’awiyah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “This matter is in the hands of the Quraysh. No one will dispute it with them except that God, the Most High, will throw him down on his face as long as they establish the religion.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Its meaning is that it is an honor for them in that it was revealed in their language. They are the most knowledgeable of it, so they should be the most upright of people in it and the most effective in implementing it. This is how their best and elite were from among the sincere ones from among the first and foremost emigrants and those who resembled them and followed them. It was said that its meaning is And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, meaning a reminder for you and your people. And singling them out for mention does not exclude others, like the Most High’s saying: “Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance. Will you not then reason?” And like His saying, the Most High, the Most Blessed: And warn your nearest relatives “and you will be questioned” about this Qur’an, and how you acted upon it and responded to it. God the Almighty said: “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: ‘Did We appoint other than the Most Merciful gods to be worshipped?’” That is, all the messengers called people to what you called people to, namely the worship of God alone, with no partner or associate, and they forbade the worship of idols and rivals, as God the Almighty said: And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities.’ Mujahid said regarding the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him: And ask those to whom We sent before you of Our messengers. Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi narrated it in this way from Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him. This is as if it is an explanation, not a recitation, and God knows best. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: “And ask them on the Night of the Isra’ Journey to Heaven, for the prophets (peace and blessings be upon them) gathered for it.” Ibn Jarir chose the first, and God knows best.

43:46: God Almighty says, informing His servant and messenger Moses, peace be upon him, that He sent him to Pharaoh and his people of princes, ministers, leaders, followers and subjects from among the Copts and the Children of Israel, calling them to worship God alone, with no partner for Him, and forbidding them from worshipping anything other than Him, and that He sent with him great signs, such as his trick and staff, and what He sent with him of the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood, and the loss of crops, lives and fruits. Despite all of this, they were too arrogant to follow and submit to them, and they denied them, mocked them and laughed at whoever brought them. And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its sister. Despite this, they did not turn away from their error and misguidance, their ignorance and their delusion. Whenever a sign of these signs came to them, they would supplicate to Moses, peace be upon him, and be gentle with him in their expression, saying: O magician, meaning the scholar, Ibn Jarir said. The scholars of their time were the magicians. Magic was not reprehensible in their time, and this was not done to diminish them, because the situation was one of necessity on their part, and it was not appropriate for that. Rather, it was to glorify them, in their opinion. Every time they promised Moses, peace be upon him, that if this were removed from them, they would believe in him and send the Children of Israel with him, and every time they broke their covenant. This is like the saying of God Almighty: “So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and the blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people. And when the punishment fell upon them, they said, ‘O Moses, call upon your Lord for us, according to what He has promised you. If you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe in you, and we will send the Children of Israel with you.’ But when We removed the punishment from them for a term they were to reach, at once they broke their covenant.”

Rather, he is the humiliated and contemptible one in creation, character and religion, and Moses is the noble, truthful, righteous and rightly guided one. His saying, and he could hardly make himself clear is also a fabrication, because even if something had happened to his tongue in his youth because of that live coal, he asked God, the Almighty, to untie a knot from his tongue so that they would understand what he was saying, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, answered him in His saying, You have been granted your request, O Moses. It is assumed that there was something left that he did not ask to be removed, as Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, but he only asked for the removal of that which would enable him to convey and understand. So, the innate things that are not the doing of the servant are not blamed or condemned for, and Pharaoh, even if he understood and had a mind, he knew this, but he only wanted to promote himself among his subjects, for they were ignorant and stupid. Similarly, his saying, Why were not bracelets of gold bestowed upon him? This is what is placed on the hands as ornaments. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Qatadah and others said: Or the angels came with him in pairs, meaning they surrounded him, serving him and bearing witness to his truthfulness. He looked at the outward appearance and did not understand the spiritual secret, which is more apparent than what he looked at if he had understood. For this reason, God the Almighty said: So he belittled his people, and they obeyed him, meaning he belittled their minds, so he called them to misguidance, and they responded to him. Indeed, they were a people of evildoers. God the Almighty said: So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him: They angered Us means they angered Us. Ad-Dahhak said on his authority: They angered Us. Ibn Abbas also said the same, as did Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, Qatadah, As-Suddi and other commentators. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ubayd God ibn Akhi Ibn Wahb told us, my uncle told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Muslim al-Tujibi, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you see God, the Blessed and Exalted, giving a servant whatever He wishes while he persists in his sins, then that is only a means of luring him into it. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all. My father told us, Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Hummani told us, Qays ibn al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: I was with Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, and sudden death was mentioned in his presence, so he said: It is a relief for the believer and a grief for the disbeliever. Then he recited, may God be pleased with him: So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all. And Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may God be pleased with him, said: I found retribution with heedlessness, meaning God Almighty’s statement: So when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all. And the Almighty said: So We made them a precedent and an example for later generations. Abu Majlaz said: A precedent and an example for those who do what they do. He and Mujahid said: And an example means a lesson for those who come after them. And God, the Almighty, is the Grantor of success, and to Him is the return and destination.
43:56: God Almighty says, informing us about Pharaoh, his rebellion, his arrogance, his disbelief and his stubbornness, that he gathered his people and called out to them, boasting and boasting about his rule over Egypt and his control over it, Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Qatada said: They had gardens and rivers of water. Do you not see? That is, do you not see what greatness and kingdom I have? He means Moses and his followers were poor and weak. This is like God Almighty’s saying: So he was gathered together and called out, * ‘I am your highest lord.’ * So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first. And his statement: Or am I better than this one who is humiliated? As-Suddi said: He means, Rather, I am better than this one who is humiliated. This is what some of the grammarians of Basra said: Am here means rather. This is supported by what Al-Farra’ related from some of the reciters that they read it as, Or am I better than this one who is humiliated? Ibn Jarir said: If this reading were correct, its meaning would be correct and clear, but it is contrary to the reading of the regions, for they read, “Or am I better than this one who is humiliated? as a question I said. In any case, what Pharaoh, may God curse him, meant by that was that he was better than Moses, peace be upon him. He lied in this statement with a clear and obvious lie, so upon him are the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection. By his statement, humiliated, he means, as Sufyan said, contemptible. Qatadah and As-Suddi said: He means weak. Ibn Jarir said: He means he has no kingdom, no authority, and no wealth. 43:57: God the Almighty says, informing us of the stubbornness of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and argument: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him. More than one person said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, and Ad-Dahhak: They laugh, meaning they are amazed by that. Qatadah said: They are alarmed and laugh. Ibrahim An-Nakha’i said: They turn away. The reason for that was what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in Al-Seerah where he said: “As far as I have been informed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting one day with Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira in the mosque, then An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith came and sat with them. In the gathering were more than one man from the Quraysh, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke, and An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith approached him, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke to him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him: “Indeed, you and what you worship other than God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it.”” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Tamimi came and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: By God, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for Ibn Abd al-Muttalib nor did he sit down, and Muhammad has claimed that we and the gods we worship are fuel for Hellfire. Abdullah al-Zubayr said: By God, if I had found him, I would have argued with him. Ask Muhammad. All that is worshipped besides God will be in Hellfire with those who worshipped it. We worship angels, the Jews worship Ezra, and the Christians worship Christ Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Walid and those who were with him in the assembly were amazed at the words of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and they saw that he had argued and argued. He mentioned that to his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Whoever loves to be worshipped besides God will be with those who worshipped Him, for they only worship Satan and the one who commanded them to worship him. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it, meaning Jesus and Ezra and those who were worshipped with them from the rabbis and monks, who passed away on…” Obedience to God, the Almighty, then those who went astray took them as lords besides God. And what is mentioned about them worshipping the angels and that they are the daughters of God was revealed: And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ Glory be to Him! Rather, [they are] [but] honored servants. The verses were revealed about what is mentioned about the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him, and that he is worshipped besides God, and Al-Walid and those present were amazed by his argument and his argument: And when he presents an example of the son of Mary, at once your people turn away from him. That is, they turn away from your command to do that from his words. Then He mentioned Jesus, peace be upon him, and said: “He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could have made from you angels on earth, succeeding [others]. And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour.” That is, the signs that were placed at his hands, such as bringing the dead back to life and healing diseases, are sufficient evidence of knowledge of the Hour. He says: “So have no doubt about them and follow Me. This is a straight path.” Ibn Jarir narrated from Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from it. He said: He meant Quraysh, when it was said to them: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be brought to it. until the end of the verses. Quraysh said to him: And who is the son of Mary? He said: He is the servant of God and His Messenger. They said: By God, he only wants us to take him as a lord, just as the Christians took Jesus, son of Mary, as their lord. God, the Almighty, said: “They do not present him to you except to argue. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim narrated to us, Shaiban narrated to us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn Aqil Al-Ansari, who said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: I learned a verse from the Qur’an that no one had ever asked me about, and I do not know whether people knew it and did not ask about it, or whether they did not realize it and asked about it. Then he began to talk to us, and when he got up, we blamed each other for not having asked him about it. I said: I will tell you about it when tomorrow comes. When the next day came, I said: O Ibn Abbas, you mentioned yesterday that there is a verse from the Qur’an that no one had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not realize it. I said: Tell me about it and about the others that you read before it. He may God be pleased with him said: Yes, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the Quraysh, O people of Quraysh, there is no good in anyone worshipped other than God. The Quraysh knew that the Christians worshipped Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon them both), and what they said about Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). They said: O Muhammad, do you not claim that Jesus (peace be upon him) was a prophet and a righteous servant of God? If you are truthful, then their gods are as they say. He said: Then God, the Almighty, revealed: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him. I said: What turn away? He said: “They laugh. “And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour.” He said: “It refers to the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon him) before the Day of Resurrection.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shaiban narrated to us, on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Abu Ahmad, the client of the Ansar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people of Quraysh, there is no good in anyone who is worshipped other than God. They said to him: Do you not claim that Jesus was a prophet and a righteous servant of God, and that he was worshipped other than God? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him. Mujahid said regarding God's statement: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him, Quraysh said: Muhammad only wants us to worship him as the people of Jesus worshipped Jesus, peace be upon him. Qatada said something similar to this. Regarding His statement: And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is he?' Qatada said: They say, Our gods are better than him. Qatada said: Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, recited: And they said, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?' meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the saying of the Blessed and Most High: They have not presented it to you except for argument, meaning disputation, and they know that it is related to the verse, because it is for something that is not rational, and it is the saying of the Most High: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire, then it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they did not worship the Messiah until they brought him, so it is clear that their statement was only disputation from them and they did not believe it to be correct. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: No people went astray after guidance they were upon except that they inherited disputation. Then the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, recited this verse: “They have not presented it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar with it, then Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic, we do not know it except from his hadith. This is what he said. It was narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, with an addition, so Ibn Abi Hatim: Humayd ibn Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Muammil narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum narrated to us, on the authority of al-Qasim Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him. Hammad said: I do not know whether it was attributed to the Prophet or not. He said: No nation went astray after its Prophet except that the first act of their going astray was the denial of predestination, and no nation went astray after its Prophet except that they were given to argument. Then he recited: “They do not present it to you except as an argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Ubad, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came out to the people while they were disputing about the Qur’an. He became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Do not compare some parts of the Book of God with others, for no people have ever gone astray without being given to disputation. Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited: “They do not compare it to you except to argue. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” And the words of God the Almighty: He is only a servant upon whom We have bestowed favor, meaning Jesus (blessings and peace of God be upon him). He is only one of the servants of God the Almighty, upon whom God bestowed the favor of prophethood and message. And We made it an example for the Children of Israel meaning evidence, proof, and evidence of Our ability to do whatever We will. And the Almighty’s statement: And if We willed, We could have made from you meaning in your place angels on the earth, succeeding you. Al-Suddi said: They succeed you in it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Qatadah said: They succeed one another as you succeed one another. This statement necessitates the first. Mujahid said: They populate the earth in your place. And the statement of the Most High: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour. Ibn Ishaq’s interpretation was presented, that what is meant by that is what Jesus, peace be upon him, was sent with, of reviving the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other ailments. There is a view on this, and more distant from it is what Qatada narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Saeed bin Jubayr, that the pronoun in and indeed refers to the Qur’an. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to Jesus, peace be upon him, as the context mentions him. Then what is meant by that is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Most High said: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death, meaning before the death of Jesus, peace be upon him, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness. This meaning is supported by the other reading: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour, meaning a sign and evidence of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said, And it is a sign of the Hour, meaning that a sign of the Hour is the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection. This is how it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Malik, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, and others. There are many hadiths on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he informed us of the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just leader and a fair judge. And the Almighty’s saying: So have no doubt about it means do not doubt that it will happen and will inevitably occur. And follow means what He has informed you about. “This is a straight path. And let not Satan avert you” means from following the truth. For indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, I have come to you with wisdom meaning with prophethood. And to make clear to you some of that over which you differ. Ibn Jarir said, He means religious matters, not worldly matters. And what he said is good and good. Then he refuted the statement of those who claimed that some here means all, and he cited as evidence the statement of the poet Labid where he said: I fight places if I do not like them or some souls cling to their doves They interpreted it as meaning all souls. Ibn Jarir said that he only meant himself, and he referred to some of them, and what he said is possible. And the statement of the Almighty: So fear God meaning in what He has commanded you, and obey in what I have brought you, "Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path" meaning, you and I are His slaves, poor, sharing in worshipping Him alone, with no partner or associate. This is a straight path meaning, what I have brought you is the straight path, which is the worship of the Lord Almighty and Exalted alone. And the statement of the Almighty: Then the parties differed among themselves meaning, the groups differed and became sects regarding him, some of them acknowledge that he is the slave and messenger of God, and he is the truth, and some of them claim that he is the son of God, and some of them say that he is God. God is far above what they say, and for this reason He says: So woe to those who do wrong from the punishment of a painful Day.

Rather, the correct view is that it refers to Jesus, peace be upon him, as the context mentions him. Then what is meant by that is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Most High said: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death, meaning before the death of Jesus, peace be upon him, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness. This meaning is supported by the other reading: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour, meaning a sign and evidence of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said, And it is a sign of the Hour, meaning that a sign of the Hour is the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection. This is how it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Malik, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, and others. There are many hadiths on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he informed us of the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just leader and a fair judge. And the Almighty’s saying: So have no doubt about it means do not doubt that it will happen and will inevitably occur. And follow means what He has informed you about. “This is a straight path. And let not Satan avert you” means from following the truth. For indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, I have come to you with wisdom meaning with prophethood. And to make clear to you some of that over which you differ. Ibn Jarir said, He means religious matters, not worldly matters. And what he said is good and good. Then he refuted the statement of those who claimed that some here means all, and he cited as evidence the statement of the poet Labid where he said: I fight places if I do not like them or some souls cling to their doves They interpreted it as meaning all souls. Ibn Jarir said that he only meant himself, and he referred to some of them, and what he said is possible. And the statement of the Almighty: So fear God meaning in what He has commanded you, and obey in what I have brought you, "Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path" meaning, you and I are His slaves, poor, sharing in worshipping Him alone, with no partner or associate. This is a straight path meaning, what I have brought you is the straight path, which is the worship of the Lord Almighty and Exalted alone. And the statement of the Almighty: Then the parties differed among themselves meaning, the groups differed and became sects regarding him, some of them acknowledge that he is the slave and messenger of God, and he is the truth, and some of them claim that he is the son of God, and some of them say that he is God. God is far above what they say, and for this reason He says: So woe to those who do wrong from the punishment of a painful Day.
43:65: God the Almighty says, informing us of the stubbornness of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and argument: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him. More than one person said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, and Ad-Dahhak: They laugh, meaning they are amazed by that. Qatadah said: They are alarmed and laugh. Ibrahim An-Nakha’i said: They turn away. The reason for that was what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in Al-Seerah where he said: “As far as I have been informed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting one day with Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira in the mosque, then An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith came and sat with them. In the gathering were more than one man from the Quraysh, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke, and An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith approached him, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke to him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him: “Indeed, you and what you worship other than God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it.”” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Tamimi came and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: By God, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for Ibn Abd al-Muttalib nor did he sit down, and Muhammad has claimed that we and the gods we worship are fuel for Hellfire. Abdullah al-Zubayr said: By God, if I had found him, I would have argued with him. Ask Muhammad. All that is worshipped besides God will be in Hellfire with those who worshipped it. We worship angels, the Jews worship Ezra, and the Christians worship Christ Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Walid and those who were with him in the assembly were amazed at the words of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, and they saw that he had argued and argued. He mentioned that to his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Whoever loves to be worshipped besides God will be with those who worshipped Him, for they only worship Satan and the one who commanded them to worship him. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it, meaning Jesus and Ezra and those who were worshipped with them from the rabbis and monks, who passed away on…” Obedience to God, the Almighty, then those who went astray took them as lords besides God. And what is mentioned about them worshipping the angels and that they are the daughters of God was revealed: And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ Glory be to Him! Rather, [they are] [but] honored servants. The verses were revealed about what is mentioned about the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him, and that he is worshipped besides God, and Al-Walid and those present were amazed by his argument and his argument: And when he presents an example of the son of Mary, at once your people turn away from him. That is, they turn away from your command to do that from his words. Then He mentioned Jesus, peace be upon him, and said: “He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could have made from you angels on earth, succeeding [others]. And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour.” That is, the signs that were placed at his hands, such as bringing the dead back to life and healing diseases, are sufficient evidence of knowledge of the Hour. He says: “So have no doubt about them and follow Me. This is a straight path.” Ibn Jarir narrated from Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from it. He said: He meant Quraysh, when it was said to them: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be brought to it. until the end of the verses. Quraysh said to him: And who is the son of Mary? He said: He is the servant of God and His Messenger. They said: By God, he only wants us to take him as a lord, just as the Christians took Jesus, son of Mary, as their lord. God, the Almighty, said: “They do not present him to you except to argue. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim narrated to us, Shaiban narrated to us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn Aqil Al-Ansari, who said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: I learned a verse from the Qur’an that no one had ever asked me about, and I do not know whether people knew it and did not ask about it, or whether they did not realize it and asked about it. Then he began to talk to us, and when he got up, we blamed each other for not having asked him about it. I said: I will tell you about it when tomorrow comes. When the next day came, I said: O Ibn Abbas, you mentioned yesterday that there is a verse from the Qur’an that no one had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not realize it. I said: Tell me about it and about the others that you read before it. He may God be pleased with him said: Yes, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the Quraysh, O people of Quraysh, there is no good in anyone worshipped other than God. The Quraysh knew that the Christians worshipped Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon them both), and what they said about Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). They said: O Muhammad, do you not claim that Jesus (peace be upon him) was a prophet and a righteous servant of God? If you are truthful, then their gods are as they say. He said: Then God, the Almighty, revealed: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him. I said: What turn away? He said: “They laugh. “And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour.” He said: “It refers to the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon him) before the Day of Resurrection.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shaiban narrated to us, on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Abu Ahmad, the client of the Ansar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people of Quraysh, there is no good in anyone who is worshipped other than God. They said to him: Do you not claim that Jesus was a prophet and a righteous servant of God, and that he was worshipped other than God? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him. Mujahid said regarding God's statement: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from him, Quraysh said: Muhammad only wants us to worship him as the people of Jesus worshipped Jesus, peace be upon him. Qatada said something similar to this. Regarding His statement: And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is he?' Qatada said: They say, Our gods are better than him. Qatada said: Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, recited: And they said, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?' meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the saying of the Blessed and Most High: They have not presented it to you except for argument, meaning disputation, and they know that it is related to the verse, because it is for something that is not rational, and it is the saying of the Most High: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire, then it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they did not worship the Messiah until they brought him, so it is clear that their statement was only disputation from them and they did not believe it to be correct. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: No people went astray after guidance they were upon except that they inherited disputation. Then the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, recited this verse: “They have not presented it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar with it, then Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic, we do not know it except from his hadith. This is what he said. It was narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, with an addition, so Ibn Abi Hatim: Humayd ibn Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Muammil narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum narrated to us, on the authority of al-Qasim Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him. Hammad said: I do not know whether it was attributed to the Prophet or not. He said: No nation went astray after its Prophet except that the first act of their going astray was the denial of predestination, and no nation went astray after its Prophet except that they were given to argument. Then he recited: “They do not present it to you except as an argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Ubad, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came out to the people while they were disputing about the Qur’an. He became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Do not compare some parts of the Book of God with others, for no people have ever gone astray without being given to disputation. Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited: “They do not compare it to you except to argue. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” And the words of God the Almighty: He is only a servant upon whom We have bestowed favor, meaning Jesus (blessings and peace of God be upon him). He is only one of the servants of God the Almighty, upon whom God bestowed the favor of prophethood and message. And We made it an example for the Children of Israel meaning evidence, proof, and evidence of Our ability to do whatever We will. And the Almighty’s statement: And if We willed, We could have made from you meaning in your place angels on the earth, succeeding you. Al-Suddi said: They succeed you in it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Qatadah said: They succeed one another as you succeed one another. This statement necessitates the first. Mujahid said: They populate the earth in your place. And the statement of the Most High: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour.
