43:66: God the Almighty says: Do these polytheists who disbelieved in the Messengers await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly while they perceive not? That is, it will inevitably happen, and these people are heedless of it and unprepared. So when it comes, it will come without them perceiving it, and then they will regret it deeply, as it will neither benefit them nor protect them. And God the Almighty says: Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous. That is, every friendship and companionship for other than God will turn into enmity on the Day of Resurrection, except for what was for God the Almighty, for it will be permanent as long as it lasts. This is like what Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said to his al-Nas 114:“You have only taken idols besides God out of affection among yourselves in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will disbelieve in one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.” Abdul Razzaq said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous. He said: Two believing friends and two disbelieving friends. Then one of the believers died and was given the good report of Paradise, so he mentioned his friend and said: O God, so-and-so is my friend. He used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger. He commanded me to do good and forbade me from evil, and he informed me that I would meet You. O God, do not lead him astray after I am gone until you show him what You have shown me and are pleased with him as You are pleased with me. Then it will be said to him: Go, for if you knew how much I have of him, you would laugh a lot and cry a little. Then the other one dies and their souls meet and it will be said: Let one of you praise the other, and each one of them will say to the other: What a good brother, what a good friend, and what a good confidant. And when one of the disbelievers dies and is given the good report of Hell, he mentions his friend and says: O God, my friend, so-and-so used to command me to disobey You and disobey Your Messenger. He commanded me to do evil and forbade me from good, and he informed me that I would not meet You. O God, do not guide him after me until you show him what you have shown me and become angry with him as you were angry with me. He said: Then the other unbeliever dies and their souls are brought together and it is said: Let each of you praise the other. Then each of them will say to the other: What a bad brother, what a bad companion, and what a bad friend! Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: Every friendship will turn into enmity on the Day of Resurrection except for the righteous. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Hisham bin Ahmad on the authority of Hisham bin Abdullah bin Katheer, Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Al-Khadir narrated to us in Ar-Raqqah on the authority of Mu’afi, Hakim bin Nafi’ narrated to us on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “If two men love each other for the sake of God, one of them in the east and the other in the west, God will bring them together on the Day of Resurrection and say: This is the one you loved for My sake.” And the saying of God, the Blessed and Exalted: O My servants, there is no fear concerning you Today, nor shall you grieve. Then He gave them good tidings, saying: Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims. That is, their hearts and inward parts believed, and their limbs and outward parts submitted to God’s law. Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman said on the authority of his father: When the Day of Resurrection comes, when the people are resurrected, not one of them will remain except terrified, then a caller will call out, O My servants, there is no fear concerning you Today, nor shall you grieve. So all the people will hope for it. He said: Then it will be followed by those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims. He said: Then the people will despair of it, except for the believers. Enter Paradise, that is, it will be said to them, Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, that is, your peers. Rejoice, that is, you will be in comfort and be happy. This was mentioned previously in Surat Ar-Rum. They will be served with trays of gold meaning yogurt, food bowls, and cups meaning drinking bowls, made of gold, without spouts or handles. And therein is whatever the souls desire Some of them read it as the souls desire “and delights the eyes” meaning pleasant food and smell and a beautiful sight. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, Ismail ibn Abi Sa’id told me that Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, told him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The lowest of the people of Paradise in station and the lowest of them in degree is a man after whom no one will enter Paradise. His sight will be expanded for him for a distance of one hundred years in palaces of gold and tents of pearls, in which there is not a space the size of a handspan that is not inhabited. He is served breakfast and dinner with seventy thousand golden trays, in which there is not a tray that does not have a color like it in the other. His desire at the end of it is like his desire at the beginning. If all the people of the earth were to descend upon him, he would be given plenty of what he was given, without that detracting from what he was given in the slightest.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junaid told us, Amr bin Sawad Al-Sarhi told us, Abdullah bin Wahb told me, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Aqeel bin Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them and mentioned Paradise, and he said: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of you will take a morsel and put it in his mouth, then another food will come to his mind, and the food in his mouth will be changed to what he desired.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and you will abide therein eternally. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan, he is Ibn Musa, told us, Sakine bin Abdul Aziz told us, Al-Ash’ath Al-Darir told us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The lowest in status of the people of Paradise is he who has seven degrees, and he is on the sixth and above him is the seventh, and he has three hundred servants and he is given breakfast and dinner every day with three hundred plates - and I do not know of anyone who did not say, ‘From gold in every A page of a color not found in another, and its beginning is as pleasant as its end. And of the drinks are three hundred vessels, each vessel of a color not found in the other, and its beginning is as pleasant as its end. And he says, O Lord, if You would permit me, I would feed and drink the people of Paradise, and nothing would be diminished from what I have. And he has seventy-two wide-eyed maidens, in addition to his wives in this world, and one of them will take a seat the length of a mile of land. And the Almighty says: “And you are therein” meaning in Paradise, eternal meaning you will not leave it nor will you seek a year from it. Then it was said to them, as a sign of favor and gratitude: And that is Paradise which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do, meaning your righteous deeds were a reason for God’s mercy to encompass you, for no one enters Paradise because of his deeds, but rather by God’s mercy and favor. Rather, degrees are attained according to the differences in righteous deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan Al-Muqri told us, Yusuf ibn Ya’qub, meaning Al-Saffar, told us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Everyone of the people of Hell will see his home in Paradise and will regret it, saying, ‘If God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.’ And every person of Paradise will see his home in Hell and will say, ‘We would not have been guided had God not guided us,’ and will be grateful.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no one who does not have a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. The disbeliever will inherit the believer’s home in Hell, and the believer will inherit the disbeliever’s home in Paradise.” This is what God Almighty said: And that is Paradise which you have inherited for what you used to do. And what God Almighty said: For you therein are many fruits, meaning of all kinds. From it you eat, meaning whatever you choose and desire. And when He mentioned food and drink, He mentioned fruit after them to complete the blessing and happiness. And God Almighty knows best.

43:81: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of those who worship Him. That is, if this were imposed, I would worship Him in that way, because I am one of His servants, obedient to all that He commands me to do. I have no arrogance or refusal to worship Him. If this were imposed, then this would be the case. However, this is impossible for Him, the Most High, and the condition does not necessarily lead to its occurrence or permissibility, as God Almighty said: “If God had willed to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills. Glory be to Him! He is God, the One, the Prevailing.” Some of the commentators said about God Almighty’s statement: Then I would be the first of those who worship, meaning the first, and among them are Sufyan al-Thawri and al-Bukhari, who narrated it and said: It is said that the first of the ungrateful worshippers is from a servant who worships. Ibn Jarir mentioned for this statement evidence what he narrated on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la on the authority of Ibn Wahb, Ibn Abi Dhi’b told me on the authority of Abu Qusayt on the authority of Ba’jah ibn Zayd al-Juhani that a woman from among them entered upon her husband, who was also a man from among them, and she gave birth to him in six months, so her husband mentioned that. To Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, so he ordered that she be stoned. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, entered upon him and said: God Almighty says in His Book, And his gestation and weaning is thirty months, and He, the Almighty, the Majestic, said, And his weaning is in two years. He said: By God, Uthman, may God be pleased with him, did not worship her until he sent for her to return. Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: A slave who refused. And the poet said: Whenever a friend wants, he can sever ties with his friend and inevitably oppress him. This statement is questionable because how does it reconcile with the condition, so that its interpretation is If this is the case, then I am abstaining from it? This is questionable, so let it be considered, unless it is said that if is not a condition, but rather a negation, as Ali ibn Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Say, ‘If the Most Gracious had a son,’ meaning: The Most Gracious did not have a son, so I am the first of the witnesses. Qatada said: It is a phrase from the speech of the Arabs: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I am the first of those who worship Him, meaning that if that does not happen, then it is not appropriate. Abu Sakhr said: “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I am the first of those who worship Him,” meaning I am the first to worship Him, as if He had no son, and the first to make Him One. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said the same. Mujahid said: Then I am the first of those who worship Him, meaning the first to worship Him, make Him One, and deny you. Al-Bukhari said: Then I am the first of those who worship Him, and both of them are words for a worshipper and a slave. The first is more likely to be a condition and a consequence, but it is impossible. Al-Suddi said: “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I am the first of those who worship Him,” meaning if He had a son, I would have been the first to worship Him, as if He had a son, but He has no son. This is the preferred opinion of Ibn Jarir and he rejected the statement of those who claimed that in is a negative. That is why God the Almighty said: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe. Meaning: Exalted and sanctified is the Creator of all things from having a son, for He is One, One, Eternal, without peer or equal, so He has no son. And the Almighty’s saying: So leave them to plunge meaning in their ignorance and misguidance and play in their world until they meet their Day which they are promised which is the Day of Resurrection. That is, they will know what their fate, their outcome, and their state will be on that day. The Almighty’s saying: And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth meaning He is the God of whoever is in the heaven and the God of whoever is on the earth, whose people worship Him and all of them are submissive to Him, humbled before Him. And He is the Wise, the Knowing. This verse is like His saying: “And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your public, and He knows what you earn” meaning He is the one called God in the heavens and the earth. And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them meaning He is their Creator and Owner, and He disposes of them without resistance or opposition. So glory and exaltation be to Him above having children, and blessed is He, meaning He is free from faults and shortcomings, because He is the Most High, the Great Lord, Owner of all things, in whose hand is the reins of all matters, whether they are to destroy or confirm. And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour meaning, none can reveal its time except Him. And to Him you will be returned meaning, He will reward each person according to his deeds, whether good or evil. Then God the Almighty said: And those they invoke besides Him meaning, idols and statues do not possess intercession meaning, they are not able to intercede for them, except for one who bears witness to the truth while they know. This is an isolated exception. That is, but whoever bears witness to the truth with insight and knowledge, then his intercession with Him will benefit him, with His permission. Then God the Almighty said: And if you ask them, 'Who created them?' they will surely say, 'God.' So how are they deluded? meaning, if you ask these polytheists who worship other than Him along with Him, Who created them?' they will surely say, 'God.' That is, they acknowledge that He is the Creator of all things alone, with no partner or associate, yet they worship other than Him along with Him, who do not own anything and are not able to do anything. In this, they are at the height of ignorance, foolishness, and mental absurdity. For this reason God the Almighty said: So how are they deluded? And the saying of God the Almighty: And his saying, ‘O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe,’ meaning, Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, his saying, meaning, he complained to his Lord about his people who denied him, so he said, O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe, as God the Almighty informed us in another verse: And the Messenger said, ‘O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur’an to be something to be abandoned.’ What we have mentioned is the saying of Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, Mujahid and Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir interpreted it based on this. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, read, And the Messenger said, ‘O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe.’ Mujahid said regarding His saying, And his saying, ‘O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe,’ he said, God the Almighty prefers the saying of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Qatadah said: It is the saying of your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), complaining about his people to his Lord the Almighty. Then Ibn Jarir narrated about the saying of God the Almighty: And his saying, O my Lord," two readings, one of them is the accusative, and it has two interpretations: One of them is that it is in apposition to the saying of God the Almighty: "We hear their secrets and their private conversations," and the second is to estimate the action and said his saying, and the second is the genitive and his saying is in apposition to his saying: "And with Him is knowledge of the Hour," and its estimation is the knowledge of his saying. And the saying of God the Almighty: "So pardon them, meaning the polytheists, and say, "Peace," meaning do not respond to them with the same bad words they address you with, but be kind to them and pardon them in action and word, for they are going to know, this is a threat from God the Almighty to them, and for this reason He unleashed upon them His punishment that cannot be repelled and made His religion and word supreme, and after that He prescribed jihad and fighting until people entered the religion of God in multitudes, and Islam spread in the East and the West, and God knows best. The end of the interpretation of Surat Az-Zukhruf.

Meaning: Exalted and sanctified is the Creator of all things from having a son, for He is One, One, Eternal, without peer or equal, so He has no son. And the Almighty’s saying: So leave them to plunge meaning in their ignorance and misguidance and play in their world until they meet their Day which they are promised which is the Day of Resurrection. That is, they will know what their fate, their outcome, and their state will be on that day. The Almighty’s saying: And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth meaning He is the God of whoever is in the heaven and the God of whoever is on the earth, whose people worship Him and all of them are submissive to Him, humbled before Him. And He is the Wise, the Knowing. This verse is like His saying: “And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your public, and He knows what you earn” meaning He is the one called God in the heavens and the earth. And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them meaning He is their Creator and Owner, and He disposes of them without resistance or opposition. So glory and exaltation be to Him above having children, and blessed is He, meaning He is free from faults and shortcomings, because He is the Most High, the Great Lord, Owner of all things, in whose hand is the reins of all matters, whether they are to destroy or confirm. And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour meaning, none can reveal its time except Him. And to Him you will be returned meaning, He will reward each person according to his deeds, whether good or evil. Then God the Almighty said: And those they invoke besides Him meaning, idols and statues do not possess intercession meaning, they are not able to intercede for them, except for one who bears witness to the truth while they know. This is an isolated exception. That is, but whoever bears witness to the truth with insight and knowledge, then his intercession with Him will benefit him, with His permission. Then God the Almighty said: And if you ask them, 'Who created them?' they will surely say, 'God.' So how are they deluded? meaning, if you ask these polytheists who worship other than Him along with Him, Who created them?' they will surely say, 'God.' That is, they acknowledge that He is the Creator of all things alone, with no partner or associate, yet they worship other than Him along with Him, who do not own anything and are not able to do anything. In this, they are at the height of ignorance, foolishness, and mental absurdity. For this reason God the Almighty said: So how are they deluded? And the saying of God the Almighty: And his saying, ‘O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe,’ meaning, Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, his saying, meaning, he complained to his Lord about his people who denied him, so he said, O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe, as God the Almighty informed us in another verse: And the Messenger said, ‘O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur’an to be something to be abandoned.’ What we have mentioned is the saying of Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, Mujahid and Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir interpreted it based on this. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, read, And the Messenger said, ‘O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe.’ Mujahid said regarding His saying, And his saying, ‘O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe,’ he said, God the Almighty prefers the saying of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Qatadah said: It is the saying of your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), complaining about his people to his Lord the Almighty. Then Ibn Jarir narrated about the saying of God the Almighty: And his saying, O my Lord," two readings, one of them is the accusative, and it has two interpretations: One of them is that it is in apposition to the saying of God the Almighty: "We hear their secrets and their private conversations," and the second is to estimate the action and said his saying, and the second is the genitive and his saying is in apposition to his saying: "And with Him is knowledge of the Hour," and its estimation is the knowledge of his saying. And the saying of God the Almighty: "So pardon them, meaning the polytheists, and say, "Peace," meaning do not respond to them with the same bad words they address you with, but be kind to them and pardon them in action and word, for they are going to know, this is a threat from God the Almighty to them, and for this reason He unleashed upon them His punishment that cannot be repelled and made His religion and word supreme, and after that He prescribed jihad and fighting until people entered the religion of God in multitudes, and Islam spread in the East and the West, and God knows best. The end of the interpretation of Surat Az-Zukhruf.
